## Read Data

```{r}
# Load necessary libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(readr)

# Read the dataset
df <- read_csv("W1 Physical Activity.csv")

# Remove non-relevant columns
df_clean <- df %>% select(-Subject, -Filename, -Epoch)

# Select only numeric columns
numeric_df <- df_clean %>% select(where(is.numeric))

# Loop through numeric columns and display density plots
for (col_name in colnames(numeric_df)) {
  p <- ggplot(numeric_df, aes_string(x = col_name)) +
    geom_density(fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.6) +
    labs(title = paste("Density Plot of", col_name),
         x = col_name,
         y = "Density") +
    theme_minimal()

  print(p)
}


```

```{r}
# Load libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(readr)

# Load the dataset
df <- read_csv("W1 Physical Activity.csv")

# Drop non-numeric columns
df_clean <- df %>% select(-Subject, -Filename, -Epoch)

# Select only numeric columns
numeric_df <- df_clean %>% select(where(is.numeric))

# Apply Shapiro-Wilk test and store results
shapiro_results <- map_dfr(names(numeric_df), function(var) {
  values <- numeric_df[[var]]
  if (length(unique(values)) < 3) {
    tibble(Variable = var, W = NA, p_value = NA, Note = "Too few unique values")
  } else {
    test <- shapiro.test(values)
    tibble(Variable = var, W = round(test$statistic, 4), p_value = round(test$p.value, 4), Note = NA)
  }
})

shapiro_results

```

```{r}
# Load libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(readr)

# Load the data
df <- read_csv("W1 Physical Activity.csv")

# Remove irrelevant columns
df_clean <- df %>%
  select(-Subject, -Filename, -Epoch)

# Ensure Age is a factor (for grouping on x-axis and coloring)
df_clean <- df_clean %>%
  mutate(Age = as.factor(Age))

# Select numeric columns excluding Age itself
numeric_vars <- df_clean %>%
  select(where(is.numeric))

# Loop through numeric variables and generate violin plots grouped by Age
for (var in names(numeric_vars)) {
  p <- ggplot(df_clean, aes(x = Age, y = .data[[var]], fill = Age)) +
    geom_violin(alpha = 0.7) +
    geom_boxplot(width = 0.1, outlier.shape = NA, fill = "white", alpha = 0.6) +
    scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Pastel1") +
    labs(title = paste("Violin Plot of", var, "by Age"),
         x = "Age",
         y = var) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(legend.position = "none")

  print(p)
}

```

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(reshape2)
library(dplyr)
library(RColorBrewer)

# Load data
data <- read.csv("W1 Physical Activity.csv")


# Compute correlation matrix
data |> 
  select(where(is.numeric)) -> df
cor_matrix <- cor(df, use = "pairwise.complete.obs")

# Melt into long format
cor_melted <- melt(cor_matrix)

# Plot heatmap
ggplot(cor_melted, aes(x = Var1, y = Var2, fill = value)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = "blue", high = "red", mid = "white",
    midpoint = 0, limit = c(-1, 1), space = "Lab",
    name = "Correlation"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 8) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, vjust = 1, hjust = 1)) +
  labs(
    title = "Correlation Heatmap of Psychometric Scores",
    x = "", y = ""
  )
```

## Scatter Plots

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(ggpubr)

data |>
  filter(Age %in% c(11, 12, 13)) |>
  mutate(Age = as.factor(Age)) |>
  select(METs, StepsCounts, Age) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = METs, y = StepsCounts)) + 
  geom_point(aes(color = Age), size = 2, alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = "black", fill = "grey70", alpha = 0.3) +  # overall best-fit line
  stat_cor(method = "pearson", label.x.npc = "left", label.y.npc = "top", size = 5) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("11" = "red", "12" = "blue", "13" = "green")) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Steps vs METs by Age Group", color = "Age")

```

## ANOVA

```{r}
# Load the data
df <- read.csv("W1 Physical Activity.csv")

# Remove 'Filename' and 'Epoch' columns
df_clean <- subset(df, select = -c(Filename, Epoch))

# Convert Age to a factor (if you want to treat it as a categorical variable)
df_clean$Age <- as.factor(df_clean$Age)

# Remove non-numeric columns other than Age
numeric_vars <- sapply(df_clean, is.numeric)
numeric_vars["Age"] <- TRUE  # keep Age for grouping
df_clean <- df_clean[, numeric_vars]

# Run ANOVA for each variable by Age
anova_results <- lapply(names(df_clean)[names(df_clean) != "Age"], function(var) {
  formula <- as.formula(paste(var, "~ Age"))
  result <- summary(aov(formula, data = df_clean))
  list(variable = var, result = result)
})

print(anova_results)

# Print results for variables with significant differences
significant_anovas <- lapply(anova_results, function(x) {
  pval <- x$result[[1]]["Pr(>F)"][1, 1]
  if (!is.na(pval) && pval < 0.05) return(x)
})



significant_anovas <- Filter(Negate(is.null), significant_anovas)

# Display variable names with significant Age effect
sapply(significant_anovas, function(x) x$variable)

```

```{r}
library(effectsize)

# Let's assume `anova_results` is as before:
effect_sizes <- lapply(names(df_clean)[names(df_clean) != "Age"], function(var) {
  formula <- as.formula(paste(var, "~ Age"))
  model <- aov(formula, data = df_clean)
  eta <- eta_squared(model, partial = FALSE)
  list(variable = var, eta_squared = eta)
})

# Filter for those with significant p-values (p < 0.05)
significant_effects <- lapply(anova_results, function(x) {
  pval <- x$result[[1]]["Pr(>F)"][1, 1]
  if (!is.na(pval) && pval < 0.05) return(x$variable)
})
significant_effects <- Filter(Negate(is.null), significant_effects)

# Pull effect sizes for only significant variables
significant_eta <- Filter(function(e) e$variable %in% significant_effects, effect_sizes)

# View the effect sizes
for (e in significant_eta) {
  cat("Variable:", e$variable, "\n")
  print(e$eta_squared)
  cat("\n")
}

```

### `kCals` and `AvgkCalsPerDay` from other data

```{r}
# Load necessary libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(tidymodels)

# Read the data
data <- read_csv("W1 Physical Activity.csv")

# --- Step 1: Drop NAs and keep only numeric predictors ---
data_clean <- data %>%
  select(where(is.numeric)) %>%
  drop_na()

# --- Step 2: Normalize and apply PCA using recipes ---
pca_recipe <- recipe(~ ., data = data_clean) %>%
  step_normalize(all_predictors()) %>%
  step_pca(all_predictors(), num_comp = 5)  # You can adjust num_comp as needed

pca_prep <- prep(pca_recipe)
pca_data <- bake(pca_prep, new_data = NULL)

# --- Step 3: Elbow method to find optimal k ---
set.seed(123)
wss_df <- tibble(k = 1:10) %>%
  mutate(
    kmeans_model = map(k, ~ kmeans(pca_data, centers = .x, nstart = 10)),
    tot_withinss = map_dbl(kmeans_model, ~ .x$tot.withinss)
  )

# Plot WSS vs K
wss_df %>%
  ggplot(aes(k, tot_withinss)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  labs(title = "Elbow Method", x = "Number of Clusters (k)", y = "Total Within-Cluster SS") + 
  theme_minimal()

# --- Step 4: Choose k (example: 3) and run k-means on PCA data ---
optimal_k <- 4  # Change this after looking at the elbow plot

set.seed(123)
final_kmeans <- kmeans(pca_data, centers = optimal_k, nstart = 25)

# --- Step 5: Add cluster labels to PCA data ---
pca_clustered <- pca_data %>%
  mutate(cluster = factor(final_kmeans$cluster))

# Optional: Visualize
pca_clustered %>%
  ggplot(aes(PC1, PC2, color = cluster)) +
  geom_point(size = 2, alpha = 0.8) +
  labs(title = "K-means Clustering on PCA-reduced Data") +
  theme_minimal()

```
